subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw doctor --fix 4-5x slower on 2026.5.20 vs 2026.5.19 (55s → 229s+) — session snapshot path traversal bottleneck

question: Should maintainers keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85670 as the canonical repair path after it fixes auth ordering and supplies live timing proof, replace it with a narrower measured repair, or close this issue only after current-release timing proves the regression is gone?
rationale: Automation cannot safely decide whether the remaining performance work is sufficiently proven or whether the open PR's auth-ordering risk is acceptable for the update/doctor path.

options.title: Repair Existing Candidate
options.body: Require https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85670 to preserve dependent auth cleanup ordering and add redacted before/after `doctor --fix` timing proof before reconsidering merge.

options.title: Replace Candidate
options.body: Close or supersede the open PR with a narrower measured repair if the sequencing risk outweighs the small parallelization benefit.

options.title: Close With Live Release Proof
options.body: If v2026.6.11 or current main no longer reproduces the reported slowdown on a comparable multi-session setup, close this issue as implemented with that timing evidence.
